newsitem.title: MALI: Mali probes deportee plane riot.
newsitem.headline: Mali probes deportee plane riot.

text.p: Mali said on Friday it had launched an inquiry into a riot on a plane repatriating expelled Malians from France and that the deportees had been detained pending investigation.
A foreign ministry statement expressed concern at the behaviour of the deportees who sacked the chartered Boeing 737 and injured 25 policemen on board -- four seriously.
The government would assume its responsibilites in the matter, the statement said.
The head of Bamako International airport where the attack occurred after landing said that one French policeman lost an eye, one had a broken arm, one a broken nose and one head injuries.

Malian security forces intervened to bring the riot under control. The plane, which was still in Bamako, had port holes smashed, the cockpit wrecked and seats ripped out. The injured were later returned to France.

The French Interior Ministry said in a statement earlier that 77 Malians, including 28 ex-convicts released from prison, were on board the plane which flew to Bamako on Thursday. On arrival, several of the Malians attacked some 40 police officers who had escorted them.

France's centre-right government has now organised 37 such charters since taking office in May 1995, pledging to crack down on illegal immigrants. Several human rights and anti-racism groups have protested at the new wave of expulsions.
